query: Which techniques prevent catastrophic forgetting during continual learning in neural networks?

documents.title: Memory retention in managed runtimes
documents.text: Garbage collection removes unreachable objects. Memory leak detectors identify retained references in application heaps.

documents.title: Dropout regularization
documents.text: Randomly disabling hidden units during training improves generalization and reduces coadaptation in neural networks.

documents.title: Elastic weight consolidation
documents.text: Continual learning can protect parameters important to earlier tasks. A Fisher information penalty discourages changes that would cause catastrophic forgetting.

documents.title: Experience replay for sequential tasks
documents.text: Rehearsing examples from earlier tasks while learning new ones helps neural networks retain earlier knowledge and avoid catastrophic forgetting.

documents.title: Deleting stored customer records
documents.text: Data retention policies specify when customer identifiers must be erased from an operational database.

documents.title: Synaptic intelligence

documents.text: MagicDNS assigns convenient names to machines connected to a tailnet.

documents.title: OAuth marketing integration
documents.text: A public campaign platform uses browser redirects to connect social media accounts.

documents.title: Private MCP authentication
documents.text: Require bearer tokens for every MCP request, store only token hashes, support revocation, and bind the server to a loopback or tailnet interface.

documents.title: Network and origin guards
documents.text: Tailnet ACLs restrict network access. An Origin allowlist prevents untrusted browser origins from calling the authenticated MCP service.

documents.title: Credential storage

documents.title: Public reverse proxy

documents.title: Removing URL trackers

documents.title: Preserving version identity
documents.text: A preprint DOI and a journal DOI identify distinct evidence records. A shared title or landing URL must not collapse their provenance.

documents.title: Explicit publication relationships
documents.text: Publisher relations such as is-preprint-of link a preprint to its published article while retaining both identifiers and source assertions.

documents.title: Editorial changes after peer review

documents.title: Printing journal issues

query: What distinguishes optimistic concurrency from database transactions using row locks?

documents.title: Counting site visits
documents.text: Analytics systems record page views and report daily visitor totals.

documents.title: Thread scheduling
documents.text: Operating systems schedule runnable threads onto processor cores.

documents.title: Optimistic concurrency control
documents.text: A transaction checks a version or timestamp before committing. A concurrent change causes the transaction to retry instead of holding a row lock throughout its work.

documents.title: Pessimistic row locking
documents.text: A SELECT FOR UPDATE operation locks selected rows. Competing writers wait until the transaction releases its locks.

documents.title: SQLite write ahead logging
documents.text: WAL allows concurrent readers while a single writer commits changes. SQLite does not offer the same row locking model as PostgreSQL.

documents.title: Browser cache expiry
documents.text: HTTP freshness directives control whether a cached resource may be reused.

query: How does an HTTP client respect 429 Retry-After and perform provider failover?

documents.title: Integer representation
documents.text: The integer 429 can be represented in decimal, binary or hexadecimal notation.

documents.title: HTTP authentication errors
documents.text: An HTTP 401 response means valid authentication credentials were not provided.

documents.title: Rate limit cooldown
documents.text: Parse Retry-After as seconds or an HTTP date, persist the account cooldown, and avoid retrying it before the indicated time after a 429 response.

documents.title: Provider fallback
documents.text: When one provider is rate limited, try a configured healthy alternative within the request deadline and report the failed provider in coverage.

documents.title: Shared provider quotas
documents.text: Accounts belonging to one quota group should share a cooldown so an exhausted team budget is not bypassed by rotating API keys.

documents.title: Rendering an error page

query: How can reciprocal rank fusion combine results whose raw scores use different scales?

documents.title: Scoring a sports tournament
documents.text: Tournament standings use wins, losses and points scored to rank competing teams.

documents.title: Cosine similarity
documents.text: Vector similarity measures the angle between query and document embeddings.

documents.title: Reciprocal rank fusion
documents.text: RRF sums one divided by a constant plus each provider rank. Using ordinal ranks avoids assuming raw relevance scores from different search engines are calibrated.

documents.title: Fusion after exact deduplication
documents.text: Merge matching evidence first and count one best rank per provider. Repeated hits from one ranked list must not inflate the fused score.

documents.title: Cross encoder reranking
documents.text: An optional cross encoder can reorder the fused candidate set using a shared relevance model after rank fusion.

documents.title: Adding measured quantities
documents.text: Adding values expressed in different units requires converting them to a compatible measurement scale.

documents.title: Durable job recovery
documents.text: Persist the provider operation ID, job status, polling cursor and partial results. After restart, resume polling rather than submitting the costly operation again.

documents.title: Worker leases and idempotency
documents.text: A restarted worker can reclaim a stale job lease. Idempotency keys and stored operation identifiers prevent duplicate submissions.

documents.title: Polling a job handle
documents.text: Clients can retrieve durable results by job identifier after reconnecting to a restarted server.

documents.title: Stopping a foreground shell process

query: How can DOI normalization preserve identity while removing resolver URL wrappers?

documents.title: Formatting author names
documents.text: Bibliographies can display initials or full given names depending on the citation style.

documents.title: General URL normalization
documents.text: Normalize host case, default ports and tracking parameters while preserving meaningful paths and query parameters.

documents.title: DOI identifier normalization
documents.text: Extract the DOI from a doi.org resolver URL or DOI label and normalize its case. The resulting DOI, rather than the resolver scheme or wrapper, identifies the record.

documents.title: Conservative DOI conflict checks
documents.text: Records with different normalized DOIs remain distinct even if a publisher landing URL matches. Identifier conflict checks protect evidence identity.

documents.title: Stable identifier aliases
documents.text: Keep a previously issued URL handle as a safe alias when an exact DOI is later obtained, unless that URL is ambiguous across conflicting DOI records.
